from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.lecture[3].set_color(owl_color)
        
        # Owl perspective label - Using Text instead of MathTex to avoid LaTeX dependency
        coord_owl = Text("(1, 1)", color=owl_color, font_size=24)
        coord_owl.next_to(mouse, UR, buff=0.1)
        
        self.play(Write(coord_owl))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.lecture[4].set_color(drone_color)
        
        # Drone perspective label (1.41 is approx sqrt(2)) - Using Text instead of MathTex to avoid LaTeX dependency
        coord_drone = Text("(1.41, 0)", color=drone_color, font_size=24)
        coord_drone.next_to(mouse, DR, buff=0.1)
        
        self.play(Write(coord_drone))
        self.wait(2)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Initial Setup
        title = "Defining a New Basis (B)"
        lines = [
            "Now, imagine a different set of basis vectors.",
            "These new vectors, b1 and b2, create a tilted grid.",
            "The space is the same, but our coordinates change."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title, lines)

        # --- Coordinate System Preparation ---
        # Standard Grid
        standard_grid = NumberPlane(
            x_range=[-4, 4, 1],
            y_range=[-4, 4, 1],
            x_length=5,
            y_length=5,
            background_line_style={"stroke_color": WHITE, "stroke_opacity": 0.2},
            axis_config={"stroke_color": WHITE, "stroke_opacity": 0.5}
        )
        self.place_in_area(standard_grid, 'A1', 'F6')

        # Basis Vectors b1=(2,1) and b2=(-1,1)
        origin = standard_grid.get_origin()
        b1_end = standard_grid.coords_to_point(2, 1)
        b2_end = standard_grid.coords_to_point(-1, 1)
        
        b1_vec = Arrow(origin, b1_end, buff=0, color="#0000FF")
        b2_vec = Arrow(origin, b2_end, buff=0, color="#FF00FF")
        
        # FIX: Replace MathTex with Text to resolve FileNotFoundError: 'latex' 
        # when a LaTeX distribution is not installed on the system.
        b1_label = Text("b1", weight=BOLD, color="#0000FF")
        b2_label = Text("b2", weight=BOLD, color="#FF00FF")
        
        # Skewed Grid
        skewed_grid = VGroup()
        b1_val = np.array([2, 1, 0])
        b2_val = np.array([-1, 1, 0])
        
        grid_range = range(-5, 6)
        for i in grid_range:
            # Lines parallel to b2
            p1 = standard_grid.coords_to_point(*(i * b1_val + -5 * b2_val)[:2])
            p2 = standard_grid.coords_to_point(*(i * b1_val + 5 * b2_val)[:2])
            skewed_grid.add(Line(p1, p2, color="#555555", stroke_width=1.5, stroke_opacity=0.8))
            
            # Lines parallel to b1
            p3 = standard_grid.coords_to_point(*(-5 * b1_val + i * b2_val)[:2])
            p4 = standard_grid.coords_to_point(*(5 * b1_val + i * b2_val)[:2])
            skewed_grid.add(Line(p3, p4, color="#555555", stroke_width=1.5, stroke_opacity=0.8))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Line: "Now, imagine a different set of basis vectors."
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(BLUE))
        self.play(Create(standard_grid), run_time=1)
        self.play(GrowArrow(b1_vec), GrowArrow(b2_vec))
        
        # Grid-based label positioning
        # b1 tip (2,1) -> C5; b2 tip (-1,1) -> C3
        self.place_at_grid(b1_label, 'B6', scale_factor=0.8) # B6 is slightly above/right of tip
        self.place_at_grid(b2_label, 'A2', scale_factor=0.8) # A2 is slightly above/left of tip
        self.play(Write(b1_label), Write(b2_label))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Line: "These new vectors, b1 and b2, create a tilted grid."
        self.play(
            self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(PURPLE)
        )
        self.play(Create(skewed_grid), run_time=2)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Line: "The space is the same, but our coordinates change."
        self.play(
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(GREY)
        )
        self.play(
            standard_grid.animate.set_stroke(opacity=0.05),
            skewed_grid.animate.set_stroke(color=WHITE, opacity=0.4)
        )
        self.wait(2)

class Section4Scene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # Background and Title

        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                # Mapping grid to the right half of the screen
                x = 1.5 + j * 0.8
                y = 1.5 - i * 0.8
                self.grid_coords[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

        mobject.move_to(self.grid_coords[grid_pos])
        return mobject

            "Mastering Change of Basis",

                "- Define Basis Vectors",
                "- Linear Transformations",
                "- Coordinate Conversion",
                "- Geometric Perspective"
            ]
        )

        # Create geometric objects for the grid
        circle = Circle(radius=0.3, color=BLUE, fill_opacity=0.5)
        square = Square(side_length=0.5, color=RED, fill_opacity=0.5)
        triangle = Triangle(color=GREEN, fill_opacity=0.5).scale(0.3)
        star = Star(n=5, outer_radius=0.4, inner_radius=0.2, color=YELLOW, fill_opacity=0.8)

        # Position objects on the right-side grid
        self.place_at_grid(circle, "A2")
        self.place_at_grid(square, "B4")
        self.place_at_grid(triangle, "D3")
        self.place_at_grid(star, "E5")

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            'To find standard coordinates, multiply matrix P by B-coordinates.',
            "Let's calculate the Owl's view for the Drone's mouse.",
            'Matrix P times the B-vector gives the standard position.',
            'Watch the mouse stay still while the grids shift.'
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Mathematical Formula & Graphical Walkthrough", lecture_lines)

        # Define Matrix P values
        p_val = np.array([[2, -1], [1, 1]])

        # Helper to create a matrix using Text to avoid LaTeX dependency
        def create_text_matrix(values, color=WHITE):
            rows = VGroup(*[
                VGroup(*[Text(str(v), font_size=24, color=color) for v in row]).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.5)
                for row in values
            ]).arrange(DOWN, buff=0.4)
            l_br = Text("[", font_size=42, color=color).stretch_to_fit_height(rows.height + 0.2).next_to(rows, LEFT, buff=0.2)
            r_br = Text("]", font_size=42, color=color).stretch_to_fit_height(rows.height + 0.2).next_to(rows, RIGHT, buff=0.2)
            return VGroup(l_br, rows, r_br)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        formula = Text("[x]_std = P * [x]_B", color=WHITE, font_size=32)
        self.place_in_area(formula, "A1", "A6", scale_factor=1.1)
        self.play(Write(formula))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        p_matrix = create_text_matrix(p_val.tolist())
        v_b_matrix = create_text_matrix([[1], [1]])
        equals_sign = Text("=", font_size=32)
        v_std_matrix = create_text_matrix([[1], [2]])
        
        calc_group = VGroup(p_matrix, v_b_matrix, equals_sign, v_std_matrix).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.3)
        self.place_in_area(calc_group, "B1", "C6", scale_factor=0.9)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(p_matrix), FadeIn(v_b_matrix))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        self.play(Write(equals_sign), FadeIn(v_std_matrix))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[3].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Demonstrating the static nature of the point in a conceptual grid
        point = Dot(color=YELLOW).scale(1.2)
        self.place_at_grid(point, "E3")
        point_label = Text("Mouse (Static Point)", font_size=20).next_to(point, DOWN)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(point), Write(point_label))
        self.wait(2)

        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section6Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Setup the title and lecture lines
        self.setup_layout(
            "Summary and Intuition Check", 
            [
                'Basis vectors are simply our chosen measuring sticks.', 
                'Transition matrices translate descriptions between different observers.', 
                'Coordinates change, but the underlying vector stays the same.'
            ]
        )
        
        # Initially dim lecture lines to focus on them one by one
        for line in self.lecture:
            line.set_color(GRAY_E)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE))
        
        t1 = Text("1. Basis = Measuring Sticks", font_size=24, color=WHITE)
        self.place_in_area(t1, "A1", "A3")
        
        # Create the grid (The 'Sticks')
        grid = NumberPlane(
            x_range=[-3, 3, 1],
            y_range=[-3, 3, 1],
            x_length=3.5,
            y_length=3.5,
            background_line_style={"stroke_color": "#444444", "stroke_width": 2},
            axis_config={"stroke_color": "#666666"}
        )
        self.place_in_area(grid, "A4", "F6")
        
        self.play(Write(t1), Create(grid))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(WHITE))
        
        t2 = Text("2. Matrix = Translator", font_size=24, color=WHITE)
        self.place_in_area(t2, "B1", "B3")
        
        # Define a transformation matrix (skew)
        skew_matrix = [[1, 0.5], [0.2, 1]]
        grid.save_state()
        
        self.play(
            Write(t2),
            grid.animate.apply_matrix(skew_matrix, about_point=grid.get_center()).set_color("#555555"),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(WHITE))
        
        t3 = Text("3. Space stays, names change", font_size=24, color=WHITE)
        self.place_in_area(t3, "C1", "C3")
        
        # Define the point (The 'Mouse') that stays fixed in absolute space
        # We calculate the point position relative to the grid center
        mouse_point = grid.get_center() + RIGHT * 0.8 + UP * 0.6
        mouse = Dot(point=mouse_point, color=YELLOW, radius=0.08)
        mouse_label = Text("The Mouse", font_size=18, color=YELLOW).next_to(mouse, UR, buff=0.1)
        
        self.play(
            Write(t3),
            FadeIn(mouse),
            FadeIn(mouse_label)
        )
        
        # Repeat the morphing animation to reinforce the takeaway
        # The grid morphs, but the Dot (mouse) stays fixed at its scene position.
        for _ in range(2):
            self.play(
                Restore(grid), 
                run_time=2,
                rate_func=slow_into
            )
            self.play(
                grid.animate.apply_matrix(skew_matrix, about_point=grid.get_center()).set_color("#555555"),
                run_time=2,
                rate_func=slow_into
            )

        self.wait(2)

outline.topic: Mastering Change of Basis: Translating Perspectives

sections.title: The Hook: The Owl and the Drone
sections.content: Introduce the concept of 'perspective' using two characters. An Owl (fixed on a branch) and a Drone (tilted and moving). They both see the same Mouse on the ground but describe its position using different numbers. This establishes that coordinates are relative to the 'basis' you choose.
sections.example: An Owl uses a standard vertical-horizontal grid, while a Drone uses a grid tilted at 45 degrees. To the Owl, the Mouse is at (1, 1). To the Drone, the Mouse is at (1.41, 0).

sections.title: Prerequisite Review: The Standard Basis
sections.content: Quick visual refresh on vectors and the Standard Basis (i-hat and j-hat). Explain that any point in 2D space is just a 'recipe' of these two unit vectors. Show a standard Cartesian grid with unit vectors i=(1,0) and j=(0,1).
sections.example: A vector v = [3, 2] is simply 3 steps along i-hat and 2 steps along j-hat.

sections.title: Defining a New Basis (B)
sections.content: Introduce a new set of basis vectors, b1 and b2. Visually show how the entire grid 'stretches' or 'rotates' when we use these new vectors instead of i and j. Emphasize that the space hasn't changed, only our 'measuring sticks'.
sections.example: Imagine a new basis where b1 = [2, 1] and b2 = [-1, 1]. Overlay this skewed grid on top of the standard square grid.

sections.title: The Transition Matrix (The Translator)
sections.content: Introduce the Change of Basis Matrix (P). Explain that this matrix acts as a 'translator' or 'dictionary'. It maps the coordinates from the new basis (B) back to our familiar standard basis (E). The columns of this matrix are simply the new basis vectors written in standard coordinates.
sections.example: If b1 = [2, 1] and b2 = [-1, 1], the transition matrix P is [[2, -1], [1, 1]]. Multiplying a coordinate from the 'Drone's perspective' by this matrix gives us the 'Owl's perspective'.

sections.title: Mathematical Formula & Graphical Walkthrough
sections.content: Present the core formula: [x]_standard = P * [x]_B. Use a split-screen animation. On the left, show the vector in the skewed B-grid. On the right, show the matrix multiplication result landing on the exact same point in the standard grid.
sections.example: If the Drone sees the Mouse at [1, 2] in its B-basis, we calculate P * [1, 2] = [[2, -1], [1, 1]] * [1, 2] = [0, 3]. The Owl sees the Mouse at [0, 3] on the standard grid.

sections.title: Summary and Intuition Check
sections.content: Summarize the three key takeaways: 1. Basis vectors are 'measuring sticks'. 2. A change of basis matrix columns are the 'new sticks' described in 'old terms'. 3. Multiplication 'translates' the description of a point from one perspective to another.
sections.example: Animate the grid morphing back and forth from square to skewed to reinforce that the 'point' (the Mouse) never moves; only our way of naming its location changes.

storyboard.title: The Hook: The Owl and the Drone
lecture_lines: Meet the Owl, watching from a steady, upright branch.
Meet the Drone, flying at a tilted forty-five degrees.
They both spot the same mouse on the ground.
The Owl sees coordinates (1, 1) on his grid.
To the Drone, that same mouse is at (1.41, 0).
animations: Fade in a grey grid (#444444) and place an Owl icon (#A52A2A) at the origin.
A yellow Mouse (#FFD700) appears at position (1, 1) on the Owl's grid.
Display coordinates '(1, 1)' in brown (#A52A2A) next to the mouse.
Overlay a cyan grid (#00FFFF) tilted 45 degrees with a Drone icon at its origin.
Display coordinates '(1.41, 0)' in cyan (#00FFFF) for the same mouse position.

storyboard.title: Prerequisite Review: The Standard Basis
lecture_lines: Usually, we describe space using the standard basis.
These are unit vectors i-hat and j-hat.
Every point is just a recipe of these two vectors.
animations: Display unit vectors i-hat (1,0) in red (#FF0000) and j-hat (0,1) in green (#00FF00).
Draw a white vector v (#FFFFFF) extending to the point (3, 2).
Flash the i-hat vector 3 times and j-hat vector 2 times to show the 'recipe'.

storyboard.title: Defining a New Basis (B)
lecture_lines: Now, imagine a different set of basis vectors.
These new vectors, b1 and b2, create a tilted grid.
The space is the same, but our coordinates change.
animations: Introduce new basis vectors b1=(2,1) in blue (#0000FF) and b2=(-1,1) in magenta (#FF00FF).
Expand a skewed grid of grey lines (#555555) based on b1 and b2.
Fade the standard grid into the background to highlight the new measuring system.

storyboard.title: The Transition Matrix (The Translator)
lecture_lines: We need a way to translate between these perspectives.
The new basis vectors form the columns of matrix P.
Think of this matrix as our mathematical dictionary.
It defines new directions using the standard grid.
These columns are the building blocks of our translation.
animations: Write matrix P = [[2, -1], [1, 1]] in white (#FFFFFF) with columns colored blue (#0000FF) and magenta (#FF00FF).
Display the text 'The Dictionary' in white (#FFFFFF) along with the dictionary icon [Asset: /mmfs1/data/home/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/dictionary.svg] above the matrix.
Animate vectors b1 (#0000FF) and b2 (#FF00FF) moving into the matrix columns.
Flash the columns of P while drawing standard basis vectors faintly (#AAAAAA) to show the 'old' terms.

storyboard.title: Mathematical Formula & Graphical Walkthrough
lecture_lines: This formula converts basis-B coordinates into standard ones.
Consider a vector at position one-two in the Drone's grid.
Multiplying by P computes the equivalent standard coordinates.
The result shows the mouse's position for the Owl.
The grid shifts, but the physical location remains fixed.
animations: Display the formula [x]_std = P * [x]_B in white (#FFFFFF) at the top.
On a skewed grid (#555555), show a vector at coordinate [1, 2] in yellow (#FFD700).
Animate matrix multiplication P * [1, 2] = [0, 3] and show vector landing at [0, 3] in yellow (#FFD700) on the standard grid.
Morph the skewed grid into the standard grid (#444444) while the vector tip remains stationary.

storyboard.title: Summary and Intuition Check
lecture_lines: Basis vectors are simply our chosen measuring sticks.
Transition matrices translate descriptions between different observers.
Coordinates change, but the underlying vector stays the same.
animations: Display '1. Basis = Measuring Sticks' in white (#FFFFFF).
Animate the grid morphing between square (#444444) and skewed (#555555) repeatedly.
Display '2. Matrix = Translator' and '3. Space stays, names change' in white (#FFFFFF).
